terminal.description: A shell in your workspace, already pointed at the offline local model.

tasks.title: Write four small graders
tasks.description:
In `src/graders.ts`, implement four factories. Each returns a `Grader`: a function from the raw model output to `{ pass, reason }`. `reason` is `''` when the grader passes and a short explanation when it fails.

- `contains(text)`: the output contains `text`, case-sensitive. A failing reason quotes `text`.
- `matches(pattern, flags = '')`: `new RegExp(pattern, flags)` finds a match. A failing reason shows `pattern`.
- `fieldEquals(field, expected)`: the output parses as a JSON object whose top-level `field` is `=== expected`. A failing reason names the field and the value it found.
- `near(field, target, tolerance)`: that field is a number no further than `tolerance` from `target`, edges included. A failing reason names the field and the value it found.

The JSON graders must never throw. When the output is not a JSON object (text around it, an array, `null`), they fail with a reason that mentions JSON.
nextSteps: Write `contains` and `matches` first; they never look inside the JSON.
Write one helper that parses the output and reads a field without throwing.
Try each grader in a scratch file on a few outputs from `node src/run.ts`.
hints: A factory is a function that returns a function. The outer one captures the settings, the inner one receives the output.
`JSON.parse` throws on text like a code fence. Wrap it in try/catch and turn the error into a failing result.
`JSON.parse('null')` and `JSON.parse('[1]')` succeed, so check the parsed value is an object that is not null and not an array before reading a field.

tasks.title: Give partial credit
tasks.description:
In `src/graders.ts`, implement `gradeOutput(output: string, graders: Grader[]): CaseGrade`.

Run every grader on the output and return:

- `score`: the share of graders that passed, from 0 to 1
- `passed`: `true` only when every grader passed
- `reasons`: the reasons of the failing graders, in grader order

A grader that throws counts as a failure whose reason starts with `grader error`, and the other graders still run. An empty list of graders throws an `Error`, because a case that checks nothing would always pass.
nextSteps: Guard against an empty list first.
Run each grader inside a try/catch.
Count the passes and collect the failing reasons.
hints: Map the graders to results first, then compute the three fields from that list.
Write a tiny `safely(grader, output)` that returns a failing result when the grader throws.
`score` is passing results divided by all results; `reasons` is the failing results mapped to their reason.

tasks.title: Compose graders per case
tasks.description:
Each case in `src/cases.ts` lists its checks as plain data (`CheckSpec`). In `src/suite.ts`, implement:

- `buildGrader(spec: CheckSpec): Grader`: `contains` uses `text`, `regex` uses `pattern` and `flags`, `field` uses `field` and `equals`, `near` uses `field`, `value` and `tolerance`. An unknown `kind` throws an `Error` that names the kind.
- `runSuite(cases: JsonCase[], model: string): Promise<SuiteReport>`: send each input through `triageJson(input, model)`, grade the reply with that case's checks and return `{ model, total, passed, meanScore, results }`. `results` holds `{ id, score, passed, reasons }` per case, in case order. `passed` counts cases where every check passed. `meanScore` is the average case score, or `0` with no cases.

The check runs hidden cases, including a reply wrapped in a code fence.
nextSteps: Loop over the cases, call the model and grade each reply.
Compute the totals, then run `node src/run.ts`.
hints: Inside each `case` of the switch, TypeScript knows which fields that spec has.
`c.checks.map(buildGrader)` gives you the grader list for one case; hand it to `gradeOutput` with the reply.
Spread the result of `gradeOutput` into `{ id: c.id, ... }` and keep the results in an array. The mean is the sum of scores over the count, guarded for zero.
